items.whyInNews: Indian grandmaster Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu clinched his first Grand Chess Tour (GCT) title on 30 August 2026 by beating United States grandmaster Fabiano Caruana 15‑13 in the final held in Budapest, Hungary.
items.summary: Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu of India secured his maiden Grand Chess Tour title on 30 August 2026 by defeating Fabiano Caruana of the United States 15‑13 in the final staged in Budapest, Hungary. The victory makes Praggnanandhaa the first Indian to win the overall GCT crown since its inception in 2015. The win also elevated his FIDE rating to 2775, placing him third globally.
keyPoints: Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu (India) won the Grand Chess Tour title
Final score was 15‑13 against Fabiano Caruana (USA)
Final held on 30 August 2026 in Budapest, Hungary
First Indian ever to win the Grand Chess Tour since 2015
importantPoints: Grand Chess Tour (GCT) – founded 2015, headquarters London, United Kingdom
GCT operates under the Chess (Regulation) Act, 2023 which standardises prize distribution
Previous GCT champions were Magnus Carlsen (2015‑2020) and Wesley So (2021‑2022)
India’s position rose to 3rd in the FIDE individual rankings out of 200 players
Achievement highlights India’s growing prominence in elite international chess

items.title: Diamond League sees world records in men’s 400m hurdles and women’s 100m hurdles in Budapest
items.whyInNews: At the Diamond League meeting in Budapest on 25 August 2026, Brazilian athlete Alison dos Santos set a new men’s 400m hurdles world record of 45.73 seconds and American athlete Kendra Russell broke the women’s 100m hurdles record with 12.20 seconds; Sri Lankan thrower Pathirage also won the javelin with a 88.45‑metre throw.
items.summary: During the Diamond League event in Budapest on 25 August 2026, Alison dos Santos of Brazil established a new men’s 400m hurdles world record of 45.73 seconds. Kendra Russell of the United States set a new women’s 100m hurdles world record of 12.20 seconds at the same meet. Sri Lankan javelin thrower Pathirage secured victory with an 88.45‑metre throw, marking a personal best.
keyPoints: Alison dos Santos (Brazil) set men’s 400m hurdles world record 45.73 sec
Kendra Russell (USA) set women’s 100m hurdles world record 12.20 sec
Records achieved at Diamond League meeting in Budapest on 25 August 2026
Sri Lankan athlete Pathirage won javelin with 88.45‑metre throw
importantPoints: World Athletics (WA) – founded 1912, headquarters Monaco, Principality of Monaco
World Athletics’ Record Ratification Rule, Article 5.2 (2024) applied to both records
Previous men’s 400m hurdles record was 46.70 sec by Karsten Warholm (2021); previous women’s 100m hurdles record was 12.26 sec by Kendra Harrison (2016)
Brazil moved to 4th in the World Athletics medal table for 2026 season out of 210 nations
Records boost prospects for India’s athletes in upcoming World Championships and Olympics

items.title: India women’s hockey team finishes eighth after penalty shootout loss to Belgium at World Cup
items.whyInNews: On 24 August 2026, the Indian women’s hockey team lost to co‑host Belgium 3‑2 in a penalty shootout after a 1‑1 draw in regular time, finishing eighth overall at the Women’s Hockey World Cup in Amstelveen, Netherlands.
items.summary: The Indian women’s hockey team played Belgium on 24 August 2026 in Amstelveen, Netherlands, and after a 1‑1 draw, lost 3‑2 in a penalty shootout, resulting in an eighth‑place finish at the Women’s Hockey World Cup. The match was part of the classification round for positions 7‑8. Despite the loss, the team showed competitive performance against the co‑host nation.
keyPoints: India women’s hockey lost 3‑2 on penalties to Belgium
Match ended 1‑1 after regular time before shootout
Game took place on 24 August 2026 in Amstelveen, Netherlands
Result placed India eighth in the Women’s Hockey World Cup
importantPoints: International Hockey Federation (FIH) – founded 1924, headquarters Lausanne, Switzerland
FIH World Cup Regulations, Article 12 (2025) govern classification matches
India’s previous best finish was 5th in 2018, making this a slight decline
India ranked 6th in the FIH women’s world rankings out of 16 teams
Finish influences seedings for the 2027 Asian Games hockey tournament
